title: 1967 Air Ferry DC-4 accident
summary: Douglas DC-4 charter flight carrying 83 passengers and 5 crew on 15-day package holiday crashed into Mount Canigó at 9,000 feet near Perpignan during descent. Aircraft had reported all well and good visibility moments before impact. French investigation determined crash resulted from series of crew errors caused by carbon monoxide poisoning from faulty cabin heater. Crew made irrational decisions and experienced language difficulties with French air traffic control, aggravating circumstances. All 88 on board killed.
probable_cause: Controlled flight into terrain caused by pilot incapacitation from carbon monoxide poisoning due to faulty cabin heater system. The faulty heater allowed carbon monoxide gas to enter the cabin, resulting in crew incapacitation and irrational behavior. Toxicological examinations confirmed carbon monoxide intoxication at levels generating amoindrissement des facultés de jugement (diminishment of judgment faculties). Contributing factors included language difficulties between crew and Perpignan controller. (p. 15, 487-488)

factors.evidence: Faulty cabin heater (Janitrol heating system) had holes and fissures in burner, allowing passage of combustion gases (burnt gases) into hot air intake ducting. Defective regulation of fuel flow or ignition system generated carbon monoxide. (p. 15, 487-488)

Toxicological examinations revealed qualitatively and quantitatively carbon monoxide intoxication in crew tissues. CO levels detected, while not producing immediately perceptible external manifestations, generated diminishment of judgment faculties and capacity. (p. 15, 488)

Crew made series of errors and irrational decisions during descent. Aircraft descended to 4,000 feet (below planned minimum safe altitude) while captain believed terrain was in view when it was not. (p. 15, 487)

Language difficulties between crew and Perpignan controller. Final communications showed hesitations in aircraft identification (confusion between Montélimar-Martigues and Montpellier) and incomprehension due to language barriers and non-standard phraseology. (p. 15, 487)

VOR (OBS) found positioned at 280° FROM (radial toward Montpellier) and channel selector displayed 112.1 or 113.1 MHz, corresponding to no frequency in Perpignan zone. Aircraft deviated progressively westward from normal P3-LR course, accumulating 15 km westward deviation by point Papa 3. (p. 15, 487)

Aircraft struck Mount Canigó at 9,000 feet at approximately 21:06 UTC (01:06 local) in descent phase. Aircraft followed wide left turn followed by 90° right turn and sharp left turn before impact at North heading. (p. 15, 488)

events.text: Aircraft reported to Perpignan ATC that all well, visibility good, beginning descent from altitude. Cockpit crew appeared normal at this time.

Faulty cabin heater (Janitrol system) continuing to release carbon monoxide gas into cabin. Crew in cockpit began experiencing effects of CO poisoning: diminishment of judgment faculties, irrational thinking, confusion.

Aircraft descended through FL 70 toward FL 50. Navigation equipment (VOR OBS) was incorrectly set to 280° FROM (Montpellier radial) instead of proper frequency. Channel selector displayed 112.1 or 113.1 MHz, which corresponded to no frequency in Perpignan zone.

Crew made series of irrational decisions and errors in descent. Communications with Perpignan ATC became hesitant with aircraft identification confusion (Montélimar-Martigues vs. Montpellier). Language difficulties and non-standard phraseology caused incomprehension between crew and controller.

Aircraft progressively deviated westward from normal P3-LR airway route after passing vicinity of Mende. Aircraft captain, despite CO poisoning effects, believed terrain was in view when it was not (visual illusion or misjudgment).

Aircraft had deviated 15 kilometers westward of planned course by point Papa 3, passed over Prades (small town) three minutes before impact. Trajectory increasingly deviated toward rising terrain due to crew's impaired navigation decisions.

Crew executed series of maneuvers apparently attempting to avoid terrain: wide left turn of approximately 2 minutes duration, then 90° right turn, then sharp left turn. Final turn was on North heading, apparently pilot attempting to avoid mountain seen with headlights. Captain had requested heading (QDM) from Perpignan.

Aircraft struck Mount Canigó during final left turn maneuver at approximately 21:06 UTC (01:06 local time), at altitude of 1,160 meters (9,000 feet), on North heading. All 88 persons aboard killed in crash. Wreckage found on mountain slope.
